Description: A rendezvous and information exchange by the piano in the Living room: after a brief private talk between Victoria Maseko and Damian Maseko, John Hobbes enters to check the piano. Damian Maseko reports the pocket watch has been recovered and mentions finding a young woman’s corpse, suspected—based on the pocket watch trail—to be Person No. 10 Eve Dauer, but not formally confirmed. Then the three hear voices and a scream from the Billiard room and rush out.
Location: Living room (Living room)
Key Information:
  - The scene takes place in the Living room (Living room). Victoria Maseko uses piano playing as a prearranged signal to rendezvous with Damian Maseko.
  - Victoria Maseko and Damian Maseko are in an intimate relationship.
  - After the piano music stops, Victoria Maseko and Damian Maseko briefly talk and confirm each other’s status.
  - John Hobbes enters the Living room and says he only wants to check the piano and will not disturb them.
  - Victoria Maseko asks whether Damian Maseko found the pocket watch; Damian Maseko says it has been recovered, but emphasizes the pocket watch itself is “not important.”
  - Damian Maseko says he found “another person” in a room; at first he thought she was just asleep, then realized it was a young woman’s corpse. The identity is not confirmed at this point.
  - A speculative inference is made from the pocket watch trail: the pocket watch was previously confirmed to be directly associated with Person No. 10 Eve Dauer, and after that there is no further clear record of No. 10’s actions. In this node the pocket watch has been recovered while the holder is unclear, and an unidentified young woman’s corpse is found, forming a time-and-item correspondence. Therefore, the young woman may be No. 10 Eve Dauer, but this judgment is only based on item association and missing timeline data, and has not been confirmed by body verification or direct identification.
  - John Hobbes adds that he found another body downstairs in the Kitchen (Kitchen), matching the previously known second-body lead.
  - The three discuss possible causes of death, including poison and unintentional death, but reach no conclusion.
  - John Hobbes mentions a police revolver hidden in Tony Dauer’s bedside table, making Tony Dauer a potential risk source.
  - In the Living room, the voices of two people can be heard in the Billiard room (Billiard room); Victoria Maseko identifies one of them as Helen Dauer.
  - A scream then comes from the Billiard room. The three immediately decide to check and rush out of the Living room together.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Enters the Living room due to the piano music and says he wants to check the piano.
    · Mentions finding another body in the Kitchen.
    · Points out a police revolver hidden in Tony Dauer’s bedside table.
    · Acts immediately after hearing the scream from the Billiard room.
  [Victoria Maseko (Victoria)] Person No. 7.
    · Was just chatting with someone in the Living room.
    · Summons Damian Maseko to the Living room by playing the piano.
    · Asks about the pocket watch and is shocked by the young woman’s corpse.
    · Identifies Helen Dauer’s voice among the voices from the Billiard room direction.
    · Urges immediate action after the scream.
  [Damian Maseko (Damian Maseko)] Person No. 8, Victoria Maseko’s boyfriend.
    · Responds to the piano signal and comes to the Living room.
    · Says the pocket watch has been recovered, but considers it less important.
    · Reports finding a young woman’s corpse, initially mistaking her for asleep.
    · Agrees after discussion that the situation no longer seems like a simple accident.
  [Eve Dauer (Eve Dauer)] Person No. 10, suspected deceased.
    · Was previously clearly recorded as being directly associated with the pocket watch.
    · After the pocket watch went missing, her personal action trail shows a clear interruption.
    · In this node, the pocket watch has been recovered and an unidentified young woman’s corpse is found, forming a correspondence in time and item clues.
    · Based on the pocket watch trail and missing timeline, she is suspected to be the young woman’s corpse, but this is not yet confirmed by direct identification or body verification.
  [Helen Dauer (Helen Dauer)] Person No. 9, not present in this node.
    · Her voice is identified by Victoria Maseko from the direction of the Billiard room.
    · Tells others to stay away from her child.
  [Tony Dauer (Tony Dauer)] Person No. 4, not present in this node.
    · Is mentioned by John Hobbes as having a police revolver hidden in his bedside table.
  [Oswald (Oswald)] Person No. 3, mentioned in this node.
    · Is considered by John Hobbes to be one of the suspicious people that night.
  [Edmund Galley (Edmund Galley)] Person No. 6, mentioned in this node.
    · Is subjectively regarded by John Hobbes as one of the suspicious parties that night.
